evidence_chain: Fact: Ichor describes itself as a designer, engineer and manufacturer of critical fluid delivery subsystems and components primarily for semiconductor capital equipment, including gas and chemical delivery subsystems that are key elements of process tools. Source: SEC FY2025 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000165253526000012/ichr-20251226.htm.

Fact: Ichor states that its gas delivery subsystems deliver, monitor and control specialized gases used in semiconductor processes such as etch and deposition; its chemical delivery subsystems blend and dispense reactive liquid chemistries used in CMP, electroplating and cleaning. Source: SEC FY2025 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000165253526000012/ichr-20251226.htm.

Fact: Ichor states that fluid delivery malfunction or material degradation can reduce yields and increase manufacturing defects, and that most OEMs outsource all or part of gas delivery subsystem design, engineering and manufacturing to a few specialized suppliers including Ichor. Source: SEC FY2025 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000165253526000012/ichr-20251226.htm.

Fact: Ichor states that early engagement with customers may allow it to design to precise specifications, be sole supplier during initial production ramp, and become preferred supplier for the full lifespan of a process tool. This is company language, not independent proof of current sole-source status on a named platform. Source: SEC FY2025 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000165253526000012/ichr-20251226.htm.

Fact: Lam Research and Applied Materials accounted for a combined 76% of Ichor's total sales in fiscal 2025; Ichor also says Lam and Applied have been customers for over 20 years, but it has no long-term contracts requiring fixed or minimum order volumes. Source: SEC FY2025 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000165253526000012/ichr-20251226.htm.

Fact: Ichor reported FY2025 revenue of $947.7 million, up 11.6% year over year, with GAAP gross margin of 9.3% and non-GAAP gross margin of 12.2%. Source: FY2025 earnings release filed with 10-K context, https://last10k.com/sec-filings/ichr/0001652535-26-000012.htm.

Fact: In Q1 2026, Ichor reported revenue of $256.1 million, up 15% sequentially from Q4 2025, GAAP gross margin of 12.6%, and non-GAAP gross margin of 12.8%. Management said the quarter benefited from a strengthening demand environment and expected another quarter of sequential improvement. Source: Q1 2026 earnings release, https://last10k.com/sec-filings/ichr/0001652535-26-000031.htm.

Fact: Ichor's Q1 2026 10-Q says semiconductor equipment spending momentum continued into Q1 2026, characterized by robust demand in its primary markets of etch and deposition, and that Q1 net sales growth reflected sustained demand from primary customers and served markets. Source: SEC Q1 2026 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000165253526000031/ichr-20260327.htm.

Fact: Ichor's Q1 2026 gross margin increased to 12.6% from 11.7% in Q1 2025; the company attributed the improvement primarily to the non-repeat of prior severance charges and increased factory utilization. Source: SEC Q1 2026 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000165253526000031/ichr-20260327.htm.

Fact: Ichor used $2.9 million of operating cash in Q1 2026, with unfavorable working-capital movement driven by increases in accounts receivable and inventory, partially offset by accounts payable. Source: SEC Q1 2026 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000165253526000031/ichr-20260327.htm.

Fact: As of June 11, 2026 10:08:59 UTC, web finance data showed ICHR market capitalization of approximately $2.50 billion, placing it in the mid-cap bucket for this funnel. Source: web finance lookup.

Inference: The combination of high Lam/Applied concentration, 20-year relationships, etch/deposition exposure, and company language about sole-supplier status during initial ramps makes Ichor a plausible subsystem chokepoint candidate, but this remains an inference until platform-specific qualifications, share data, or named design wins are verified.

Hypothesis: AI-driven leading-edge WFE demand can flow into Ichor through OEM etch/deposition platforms, but Q1 2026 disclosures do not yet isolate AI, HBM, leading-edge logic, or a specific tool platform as the driver.
falsification_plan: Downgrade if revenue growth tracks only generic WFE recovery while Ichor provides no evidence of new platform wins, qualification progress, or share gains at Lam/Applied.
Downgrade if top-customer concentration falls because Lam or Applied shift share away from Ichor rather than because Ichor diversifies into new OEMs or non-semi markets.
Downgrade if Q2-Q4 2026 revenue rises but GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins fail to improve, suggesting weak pricing power, poor absorption, or costly ramp execution.
Downgrade if inventories and receivables continue to rise faster than revenue without later cash conversion, implying working-capital drag rather than chokepoint economics.
Downgrade if OEM commentary or procurement evidence indicates aggressive dual-sourcing, redesign around Ichor modules, or shorter qualification cycles than assumed.
Downgrade if etch/deposition demand at Lam/Applied weakens while Ichor cannot offset with wet-process, ASML, aerospace/defense, medical, or commercial-space growth.

Upgrade only if primary sources show named platform qualification, sole/dual-source status, preferred-supplier status, design-win language, or sustained margin expansion tied to higher utilization and mix rather than one-time cost actions.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: The hidden signal is not broad WFE commentary; it is whether Ichor is sole-sourced, dual-sourced, or preferred-sourced on specific Lam Research or Applied Materials etch/deposition platforms, and whether Q2-Q4 2026 revenue growth is accompanied by clean-room/factory utilization improvement, non-GAAP gross-margin expansion, and stable or rising share at top OEM customers.

Map Ichor product categories to OEM platforms: gas delivery subsystems, chemical delivery, weldments, precision machining, advanced flow controller, valves and specialty joining.

Track restructuring execution after the Scotland/Korea closure and machining-asset relocation; verify whether footprint consolidation improves utilization and gross margin.
Investigate patents and product literature around Ichor's advanced flow controller and mass-flow replacement claims; assess whether this is a real differentiated component or a small product feature.

Interview-style diligence checklist: ask whether customers can qualify an alternate supplier in months or years, whether Ichor owns process know-how or merely builds to print, and whether pricing resets during ramps.
risks: Customer concentration risk: Lam Research and Applied Materials represented 76% of FY2025 sales; this can be evidence of integration but also creates bargaining-power and order-volatility risk.
No guaranteed volume: Ichor discloses that it does not have long-term contracts requiring customers to place fixed or minimum order quantities.
Cyclicality risk: semiconductor capital equipment is inherently cyclical; revenue recovery could reflect broad WFE restocking rather than defensible platform share.
Pricing-power risk: major OEM customers may require reduced prices or delivery/quality commitments, pressuring gross margin even if volume rises.
Evidence gap: no public source in this evidence set proves Ichor is sole-sourced or dual-sourced on a named Lam or Applied platform today.
Working-capital risk: Q1 2026 operating cash flow was negative as receivables and inventories increased during the ramp.

Tariff/export-control risk: Ichor identifies global tariffs and U.S. export controls, especially around advanced semiconductor technology and China, as factors that could affect demand, costs and supply chain operations.
Execution risk: restructuring and manufacturing footprint rationalization may improve utilization, but could also disrupt capacity, quality, or delivery performance if poorly executed.
Margin-quality risk: Q1 2026 margin improvement was partly due to non-repeat of severance charges; sustained improvement must be separated from temporary cost effects.

Substitution/internalization risk: OEMs could dual-source more aggressively, redesign modules, or internalize subsystem work if supply-chain resilience becomes more important than outsourcing efficiency.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: AI compute demand -> leading-edge logic/HBM/advanced-node capacity -> wafer fab equipment capex -> etch/deposition/wet-process tools from OEMs such as Lam Research, Applied Materials, ASML and peers -> outsourced fluid delivery subsystems -> gas boxes, chemical delivery modules, weldments, precision machining, valves/flow-control components -> Ichor manufacturing footprint in the U.S., Malaysia, Mexico and other facilities. CN: Ichor 位于前道设备 OEM 内部子系统层，不直接卖 AI 芯片或服务器，而是通过刻蚀、沉积、清洗、CMP 等制程设备需求间接受益。
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：Ichor 可能不是普通周期性半导体设备零部件供应商，而是嵌入 Lam Research、Applied Materials、ASML 等前道设备 OEM 平台的气体与化学液体输送子系统供应商。其气体输送子系统用于刻蚀、CVD、PVD、外延、strip、光刻等 dry process 工具；化学液体输送产品用于 wet clean、电化学沉积、CMP 等 wet process。若 Ichor 在具体下一代平台上早期参与设计、完成客户认证，并在初始量产爬坡阶段成为 sole supplier 或 preferred supplier，则客户切换成本、验证周期和质量风险可能使其具备一定瓶颈属性。当前证据支持“值得深挖”，但尚不足以证明其在某些 Lam/Applied 平台上具有不可替代或长期独占地位。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: Ichor may be more than a generic cyclical semiconductor-equipment supplier; it may be a qualified gas and chemical delivery subsystem vendor embedded inside OEM tools from Lam Research, Applied Materials, ASML, and others. Its gas delivery subsystems are used in dry-process tools such as etch, CVD, PVD, epitaxy, strip, and lithography, while its chemical delivery products serve wet clean, electrochemical deposition, and CMP. If Ichor is designed in early, qualified on next-generation platforms, and becomes sole or preferred supplier during initial ramps, the validation burden, yield-risk implications, and OEM switching cost could make the role more chokepoint-like. Current evidence supports a deep-research candidate, but does not yet prove platform-specific sole-source or durable share lock-in.
deep_reports.title_cn: Ichor：前道设备气体/化学液体输送子系统的低关注度卡点假设
deep_reports.title_en: Ichor: Underfollowed Fluid-Delivery Subsystem Chokepoint Hypothesis in WFE
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: Ichor is screened and categorized as a small/mid-cap cyclical semiconductor capital-equipment supplier, which can obscure a narrower question: whether customer-qualified fluid delivery subsystems are sticky once designed into specific OEM process tools. Customer concentration also screens as a risk, but in the Serenity chokepoint framework it may be dual-use evidence: risk if pricing power is weak, but a possible signal of deep platform integration if paired with long qualification, design-in wins, and margin recovery.

evidence_chain: Hypothesis from provided brief: Ultra Clean may occupy a hidden bottleneck in contamination-sensitive semiconductor equipment supply chains where certified cleaning, analytical services, and subsystem assembly become harder to replace as process tolerances tighten.

Fact from provided external context: The broader HBM and advanced-packaging research frame argues that the market has already identified many obvious HBM producers and direct suppliers, so the underfollowed search should move one or two layers beneath the obvious beneficiaries.

Inference: UCTT fits the two-lane Serenity funnel as an underfollowed candidate because it sits below the more visible AI semiconductor and WFE names, closer to qualified manufacturing, cleaning, and service execution than to the headline AI compute layer.
Hypothesis: If services revenue is material and margins remain resilient through WFE cycles, UCTT may have more chokepoint characteristics than a normal outsourcing vendor.
Hypothesis: If customer qualification cycles are long, switching costs are high, and contamination-control standards tighten with advanced nodes, UCTT’s role may carry hidden durability.

Evidence gap: The current evidence package does not yet include UCTT’s latest segment revenue split, customer concentration, named customer commentary, service margin disclosure, clean-room utilization, or management statements explicitly tying demand to advanced-node complexity.

Inference: The most important near-term evidence is not headline revenue growth alone, but the mix and quality of growth: services versus product/subsystem revenue, gross margin by activity, operating leverage, working-capital conversion, and customer durability.
falsification_plan: Falsify or downgrade the thesis if latest filings show services revenue remains immaterial relative to product/subsystem assembly.
Falsify or downgrade if service gross margins are not meaningfully more resilient than product margins across cycle conditions.
Falsify or downgrade if customer disclosures show excessive dependence on one or two OEMs without evidence of durable qualification or switching friction.

Falsify or downgrade if management commentary frames recovery only as generic WFE cyclicality, with little evidence of advanced-node, HBM, AI accelerator, or contamination-control complexity as demand drivers.
Falsify or downgrade if clean-room capacity is abundant, easily replicated, or underutilized despite market recovery.
Falsify or downgrade if revenue growth consumes cash through inventory, receivables, or capex without margin expansion.
Falsify or downgrade if competitors or customers demonstrate that certified cleaning, analytical services, or subsystem assembly can be easily multi-sourced.
Falsify or downgrade if market-pricing checks show the stock already embeds a high-quality services multiple without supporting evidence.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether UCTT has durable qualification lock-in with major semiconductor equipment OEMs such as Applied Materials, Lam Research, or other WFE customers; whether services revenue and margins are more resilient than product/subsystem assembly; whether clean-room capacity and utilization are constrained; and whether management links demand to advanced-node process complexity rather than only a generic WFE cycle recovery.

Check whether UCTT discloses clean-room capacity additions, facility expansions, regional manufacturing footprint, or utilization commentary; map this against semiconductor equipment cycle timing.

Compare UCTT against peers in precision cleaning, subsystem assembly, and semiconductor equipment services to determine whether its margin profile indicates true differentiation or commodity outsourcing.

Set monitoring triggers: services revenue growth versus product revenue growth, segment margin spread, customer concentration changes, clean-room utilization, capex intensity, inventory build, and free-cash-flow conversion.

risks: Services mix may be too small to influence consolidated economics, leaving UCTT primarily exposed to lower-margin cyclical subsystem assembly.
Revenue recovery may come mainly from WFE volume normalization rather than from advanced-node contamination-control complexity.
OEM qualification may be less durable than assumed if customers can rebid work, dual-source aggressively, or internalize sensitive processes.
Customer concentration could create bargaining-power risk if a small number of WFE OEMs control pricing, volumes, and payment terms.
Margin recovery could lag revenue growth, suggesting limited pricing power and weak chokepoint economics.
Clean-room capacity additions could require capex ahead of demand, reducing free cash flow during cyclical upturns.

If the semiconductor equipment cycle weakens, UCTT may still trade and operate like a cyclical supplier even if the long-term process-complexity thesis is directionally correct.

deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Technology → AI compute and advanced semiconductors → advanced-node logic, HBM, and AI accelerator manufacturing → wafer fab equipment OEMs → qualified subsystem suppliers and contamination-control service providers → Ultra Clean. UCTT appears positioned one layer beneath the obvious WFE leaders: it may support equipment OEMs through clean manufacturing, subsystem integration, precision cleaning, analytical services, and contamination-control workflows. Reference leaders in the broader chain include semiconductor equipment OEMs and HBM/advanced packaging beneficiaries, but the underfollowed angle is the qualified cleanliness and service node beneath them.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：Ultra Clean 可能不是普通的半导体设备外包制造商，而是处在先进制程、HBM、AI 加速器和复杂 WFE 设备扩张中更难替代的洁净制造、超高纯清洗、分析服务和子系统装配节点。随着制程容忍度收紧，污染控制、洁净室能力、客户认证和服务质量的重要性可能上升。市场可能仍按周期性外包制造商给 UCTT 定价，而没有充分区分其服务收入韧性、OEM 认证壁垒和污染敏感型子系统能力。该判断目前仍为 hypothesis，需要用最新 10-K/10-Q、earnings call、客户集中度、产品/服务收入拆分、服务毛利率、产能利用率和先进节点相关披露来验证。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: Ultra Clean may be more than a cyclical outsourced manufacturing vendor for semiconductor equipment. It may occupy a qualified, contamination-sensitive supply-chain node spanning ultra-clean manufacturing, ultra-high-purity cleaning, analytical services, and subsystem assembly for major semiconductor equipment OEMs. As process tolerances tighten in advanced nodes, HBM, AI accelerators, and complex WFE tools, contamination control and qualified clean-room execution may become harder to replace. The market may still screen UCTT as a cyclical outsourcing name rather than a qualified service and subsystem partner. This remains a hypothesis, not a proven chokepoint, and must be verified through the latest filings, earnings calls, customer concentration, product-versus-service mix, services margin resilience, clean-room utilization, and advanced-node commentary.

deep_reports.why_underfollowed: UCTT can be overlooked because its surface label resembles outsourced manufacturing or cyclical semiconductor capital-equipment support, which sounds lower quality and lower moat than the possible reality of qualified contamination-sensitive manufacturing and services. It is also one or two steps removed from the obvious AI winners: investors tend to focus first on GPUs, HBM producers, advanced packaging, and WFE OEMs, while lower-profile service, cleaning, analytical, and subsystem partners receive less attention. The underfollowed signal is not simply small size; it is the possible mismatch between a low-glamour industry label and a potentially qualification-heavy, contamination-control role.

evidence_chain: Fact from provided brief: The target company is FormFactor Inc. with ticker FORM, classified as a mid-cap, underfollowed discovery-lane candidate with low attention.

Fact from provided brief: The stated chokepoint hypothesis is that AI accelerators, HBM, chiplets, and advanced packaging increase wafer-probe and probe-card complexity, potentially making test interfaces a production-yield bottleneck.

Fact from provided brief: Required verification fields include HBM/AI exposure, probe-card demand, customer concentration, memory versus foundry/logic exposure, gross-margin mix, and longer or more customer-specific qualification cycles.

Fact from external search context: The HBM supply-chain article argues that HBM producers are structurally undersupplied through 2027 and that a research lens should examine sub-$50B suppliers one layer below producers, while also warning that the market has already identified much of this layer. Source: https://outperformers.co/p/tss3

Inference: If HBM and advanced-packaging capacity additions require more complex wafer-level testing and customer-qualified probe cards, FORM may have more direct AI/HBM leverage than its generic semiconductor-test label suggests.

Inference: If revenue and margin growth are concentrated in high-end probe-card applications tied to HBM, AI accelerators, foundry/logic, or HPC, the thesis quality would improve from early hypothesis toward supported chokepoint candidate.

Hypothesis: FORM’s qualification cycles and customer-specific platforms could create switching friction, making share more durable than a normal hardware cycle. This must be verified through filings, call transcripts, customer concentration, and product-level disclosures.

Speculation: The market may still underprice FORM if investors categorize it as cyclical test equipment rather than as a scarce interface supplier for advanced memory and logic yield ramps. This remains speculative until valuation, consensus estimates, analyst coverage, and segment data are checked.
falsification_plan: Falsify if management commentary, filings, or call transcripts show no meaningful HBM, AI accelerator, HPC, foundry/logic, or advanced-packaging linkage behind recent growth.
Falsify if probe-card order growth is broad-based across mature nodes or memory recovery rather than concentrated in high-complexity applications.
Falsify if gross margin fails to improve, or declines, during periods when high-end probe-card demand is supposedly increasing.
Falsify if customer concentration disclosures or industry checks indicate share loss at key HBM, DRAM, foundry, or HPC customers.
Falsify if competitors show stronger evidence of HBM/AI probe-card wins, shorter lead times, better margins, or superior customer qualification status.
Falsify if advanced-packaging test economics accrue mainly to testers, OSATs, inspection/metrology vendors, or captive customer platforms rather than probe-card suppliers.
Falsify if backlog, bookings, or management commentary indicate normalization after a short cyclical restocking period instead of sustained structural demand.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether HBM and AI accelerator production ramps are causing a mix shift toward more complex, higher-value probe cards and wafer-probe solutions at FORM, evidenced by HBM/AI/HPC commentary, memory versus foundry/logic growth, probe-card bookings, customer-specific qualifications, gross-margin expansion from high-end mix, and resilience relative to broader semiconductor test cycles.
next_research_tasks: Pull FORM’s latest 10-K, 10-Qs, investor presentations, and earnings-call transcripts; extract all mentions of HBM, AI, HPC, advanced packaging, DRAM, foundry/logic, probe cards, wafer probe, qualification, and customer-specific platforms.
Build a revenue bridge by segment and end market: memory versus foundry/logic, systems versus probe cards, and any disclosed advanced-node or high-performance-computing exposure.
Check whether gross margin changes correlate with management commentary on high-end probe-card mix, memory strength, advanced packaging, or AI-related demand.

Analyze customer concentration disclosures over the last five years and map likely exposure to major HBM producers, foundries, and AI accelerator supply chains without assuming customer identities unless disclosed.

Compare FORM with reference and peer companies in semiconductor test, probe cards, and wafer-probe systems to determine whether FORM has differentiated HBM/AI exposure or is merely participating in sector recovery.
Review industry sources on HBM capacity additions, advanced-packaging ramps, and probe-card technical requirements to determine whether test-interface complexity is rising structurally.

Check sell-side coverage count, institutional ownership, market-cap history, liquidity, and valuation multiples to test whether FORM is genuinely underfollowed or already priced as an AI/HBM beneficiary.
Create a quarterly monitoring dashboard for HBM/AI commentary, probe-card bookings, backlog, memory/foundry mix, gross margin, customer concentration, and any signs of share gains or losses.
risks: Cyclical false positive: order growth may reflect broad semiconductor recovery rather than structural HBM, AI accelerator, or advanced-packaging demand.
Evidence gap: FORM may not disclose enough HBM, AI, HPC, or advanced-packaging revenue detail to separate chokepoint exposure from generic probe-card sales.
Competition risk: higher probe-card complexity may attract or strengthen competitors, compressing margins despite demand growth.
Customer concentration risk: if a small number of memory or foundry/logic customers drive demand, share loss or delayed capex at one customer could materially weaken the thesis.

Value migration risk: advanced packaging could shift more test value toward other tools, outsourced semiconductor assembly/test vendors, package-level test platforms, or vertically integrated customer solutions.

Market-recognition risk: the external context warns that the market has already identified many suppliers one layer below HBM producers, so FORM may be less mispriced than the underfollowed label implies.
Margin-risk mismatch: if high-end probe-card mix rises but gross margin does not improve, the supposed complexity premium may be weaker than expected.
Qualification-cycle downside: long certification cycles can create defensibility, but they can also delay revenue conversion and make share shifts hard to detect until late.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: AI compute demand -> HBM and advanced logic/chiplet production -> wafer-level testing and yield learning -> probe stations, probe cards, test interfaces, thermal/electrical contact systems -> customer-specific qualification at memory, foundry/logic, and advanced-packaging customers. FORM sits below the obvious AI accelerator and HBM producers, at the interface where advanced wafers/packages must be electrically contacted and tested before yield ramp and volume production. Reference leaders include AI compute vendors, HBM producers, foundries, and advanced-packaging capacity owners; FORM is the underfollowed supplier-level candidate one layer below those leaders.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：FormFactor 可能受益于 AI 加速器、HBM、chiplet 和先进封装带来的测试复杂度提升。核心逻辑不是“半导体设备周期复苏”，而是高端晶圆探针、探针卡和测试接口可能成为先进存储与高性能逻辑量产爬坡中的合格接口瓶颈。若 HBM、AI accelerator、foundry/logic 与 advanced packaging 相关收入占比提升，并带动探针卡订单、毛利率和客户认证壁垒改善，则 FORM 的业务属性可能从普通测试硬件供应商上修为先进制程/先进封装良率爬坡的关键节点。当前结论级别：hypothesis，需要财报、电话会、客户结构和订单/毛利证据验证。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: FormFactor may benefit as AI accelerators, HBM, chiplets, and advanced packaging raise the complexity of wafer probe, probe cards, and test interfaces. The core question is not simply whether semiconductor test spending recovers cyclically, but whether high-end probe cards are becoming scarce, qualified interfaces needed for yield learning and production ramps in advanced memory and high-performance logic. If HBM, AI accelerator, foundry/logic, and advanced-packaging exposure is rising and is visible in probe-card demand, gross margin mix, bookings, and customer qualification strength, FORM could deserve to be researched less as generic test hardware and more as a yield-ramp chokepoint. Current confidence level: hypothesis, pending filings, earnings-call, customer, order, and margin verification.

deep_reports.why_underfollowed: The market may miss the signal because semiconductor test hardware sounds cyclical, downstream, and less strategically important than GPUs, HBM producers, foundries, or packaging equipment. The underfollowed angle is that probe cards and wafer-probe interfaces may become more specialized as HBM stacks, chiplets, and advanced packages increase pin density, thermal constraints, signal-integrity requirements, and customer-specific qualification burdens. However, this is not a hidden mega-discovery: the supplied external context on the HBM supply chain says the market has largely identified many sub-$50B suppliers one layer beneath HBM producers, so the research edge must come from proving that FORM has unusually direct, durable, margin-accretive exposure rather than generic semiconductor beta.
